accepted.reason: Reasonable incremental change from the current SIR|obs=I baseline: adding E can better capture sharp, high-peaked single-season waves without introducing an explicit H compartment that is flagged as weakly identifiable. Complexity remains moderate and typically identifiable with one observed series compared to adding additional unobserved pathways.

Observation-target alignment is improved versus obs=I because hospitalization admissions plausibly lag infections; a 1-week delayed_I map matches the surveillance semantics and avoids adding an explicit H compartment. However, with only 31 training weeks, the fixed delay can still be sensitive/weakly supported and may trade off with transmission/clearance parameters, so it is less robust than proposal 0.

rejected.reason: Over-complex for a single observed hospitalization-rate series when still mapping observations to I: adding an asymptomatic compartment (A) increases parameterization and introduces substantial identifiability risk (I vs A tradeoffs) without improving observation-target alignment (hospitalizations are not directly I). Likely to be unstable across splits for short single-season data.

suggested_edits.edit: Consider switching observation_map from I to delayed_I with delay_weeks=1 to better align with hospitalization-rate semantics while keeping the SEIR structure unchanged; avoid adding an explicit H compartment given identifiability concerns in short single-season data.

If retained, keep delay fixed (as proposed) and avoid adding additional compartments; consider also evaluating delay_weeks=0 vs 1 within the same structure during fitting to reduce risk that an unsupported lag drives parameter compensation.

If SEIAR must be considered, change observation_map to delayed_I (with a small fixed delay) to better match hospitalization-rate semantics; otherwise prefer simpler SEIR/SIR variants due to identifiability risk from the added A pathway.
